text:
javier: Quick check — noticed model-configmaps sometimes mount old values after terraform apply. Pods don't restart even though CM updated. Is TF provider apply ordering to blame? Anyone seen this? cc @marta @kevin

marta: We hit this before. TF will create/update the ConfigMap but k8s won't restart pods automatically. The typical solution is a checksum annotation on the deployment pod template so any CM change forces a rollout.

kevin: +1. Pattern I use:
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    checksum/config: "{{ md5(file("./configs/my-model.yaml")) }}"
```
TF will change the annotation when the source file/hash changes, which mutates podTemplate and triggers a rollout.

lina: The complication: our per-model CMs are generated by the operator (not from a local file), so we don't have a local file to hash. Operator writes the CM after TF runs — can race if TF applies CM and deployment in same run.

marta: If the operator owns the CM, operator should handle rollout (patch deployment with checksum derived from CM or trigger restart). Do we have operator doing that today? @kevin

kevin: Operator currently only updates the CM data, it doesn't patch deployments. Short-term workarounds: configmap-reload sidecar, init container that waits for checksum, or add a TF post-apply step to touch deployment annotation.

javier: For a quick hotfix I can add a null_resource in TF to patch the deployment annotation after CM updates. Ugly but fast. Example:
```hcl
resource "null_resource" "poke_deploy" {
  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "kubectl annotate deploy/model-deploy checksum/config=$(kubectl get cm model-config -o jsonpath='{.data.config}' | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1) --overwrite"
  }
  triggers = { cm_version = kubernetes_config_map.model_config.metadata[0].resource_version }
}
```

lina: Fine as short-term. Long-term we should either: 1) add operator behavior to patch/deploy, or 2) have TF create an explicit roll-trigger job that waits for the CM to be fully reconciled before touching deployment. I opened a ticket: https://rwd/issue/INFRA-789

ops-bot: deploy-bot: applied terraform plan 2026-03-17T14:05:22Z — plan succeeded, no changes to deployment.

marta: Also flag: if the CM data includes secrets (Vault sync), the secret syncer can lag and the CM checksum may not reflect final runtime values. In that case consider projecting secrets into volumes or ensuring secret sync completes before the rollout trigger.

kevin: TL;DR: short-term = null_resource patch or TF post-apply annotate; medium = operator patches deployment on CM change; long-term = kube-native reload sidecar + improved secret sync.

javier: Thanks all — I'll push the null_resource change now and follow up on INFRA-789.
